title: RFID Reader And Card Encoding Buyer's Guide
summary: This page is for teams choosing RFID readers, USB encoders or test benches and still deciding which protocol, SDK support and operating workflow fit the real enrollment or issuance job.
heroPoints: Protocol and software environment should drive the first shortlist before reader form factor does.
A reader is only a fit if it matches the cards, tags and host workflow the team actually uses.
The best pilot validates drivers, SDK behavior and card handling together, not in separate steps.

faq.question: What should decide the first RFID reader shortlist?
faq.answer: The first shortlist should come from the exact card or tag family, host environment and integration workflow the team needs to support rather than from the reader brand or enclosure style alone.

faq.question: Why do reader projects stall so often after purchase?
faq.answer: They often stall because teams choose hardware before defining the software environment, the real credential set and the operating workflow the reader must support.

sources.label: ISO/IEC 18000-63 — UHF Gen2 air interface (860–960 MHz)
sources.note: UHF Gen2 air-interface specification reader vendors must implement for RFID encoding and inventory reads.

sources.label: ISO/IEC 14443 — Proximity cards (Parts 1–4)
sources.note: HF proximity air-interface specification implemented by desktop encoders, card-readers and mobile encoders.

sources.label: ISO/IEC 15693 — Vicinity cards (13.56 MHz)
sources.note: HF vicinity air-interface specification implemented by library, laundry and long-range HF encoders.

sources.label: GS1 EPC Tag Data Standard (TDS) 2.1
sources.note: Canonical EPC encoding scheme reference for SGTIN, GIAI and GRAI encoding on UHF readers.

sources.label: EPCglobal Low-Level Reader Protocol (LLRP) 1.1
sources.note: Reader-to-host protocol that governs integration of UHF RFID readers and encoders into middleware.

sources.label: Impinj R700 — UHF RFID reader
sources.note: Flagship fixed UHF reader cited across RFID reader-and-encoding deployments.

sources.label: Zebra FX9600 — fixed UHF RFID reader
sources.note: High-performance fixed UHF reader cited in warehouse and inventory encoding stations.
